release: Romans four additional God referent and divine quotation corrections after full Acts–Revelation release

changes.before: and being fully assured that what he had promised, he was able also to perform.
changes.after: and being fully assured that what God had promised, God was able also to perform.
changes.reason: In Romans 4:20–21 the promise was made by God; Avraham is the one assured of it.

changes.before: So then, he has mercy on whom he desires, and he hardens whom he desires.
changes.after: So then, God has mercy on whom God desires, and God hardens whom God desires.
changes.reason: Romans 9:15–19 repeatedly names God as the one who has mercy or hardens.

changes.before: Again he says, "Rejoice, you Gentiles, with his people."
changes.after: Again Scripture says, "Rejoice, you Gentiles, with God’s people."
changes.reason: Romans 15:9–11 quotation sequence: the scriptural citation has the Gentiles rejoicing with the people of God. Speaker of “Again” is Scripture, not an implicit male God.

changes.before: Again, "Praise the Master, all you Gentiles! Let all the peoples praise him."
changes.after: Again, "Praise the Master, all you Gentiles! Let all the peoples praise the Master."
changes.reason: The Master in this cited invitation to praise is God, not Yeshua, so use the established title twice.
